title: Internet Clock
intro: Get the exact time from the internet and show it on an OLED screen.

steps.title: Join the WiFi
steps.text:
This time your board joins a WiFi network that has the internet. `WiFi.begin(name, password)` starts joining; the `while` loop waits until it's connected.

**Your task:** type in the WiFi name and password (ask your teacher), then Upload. (In the simulator, any name works.)
hints: The name and password go inside the quotes, exactly as written: capitals matter.
If the dots go on forever, the name or password is wrong, or the network blocks devices like yours.
ESP boards only use 2.4 GHz WiFi networks.

steps.title: Ask for the time
steps.text:
**NTP** (Network Time Protocol) asks a time server for the exact time. `configTime` starts it. `TZ` sets the time zone: Melbourne is 10 hours ahead of world time, 11 in summer.

`localtime_r` splits the time into hours (`tm_hour`), minutes (`tm_min`) and seconds (`tm_sec`).

**Your task:** fill in the blank to print the minutes too.
steps.success: The exact time, from the internet!

steps.title: The clock
steps.text: **Goal:** show the time in big numbers on the OLED, updating every second, like `14:05:09`. Show `Connecting...` while it joins the WiFi.
hints: `snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%02d:%02d:%02d", ...)` makes text with two digits each, like 09.
Clear the screen, print, then `display.display()` every time.

checks.label: It shows hours, minutes and seconds
My clock shows the right time

steps.success: An internet clock! It'll stay right to the second.

outro: Your clock asks a **time server** on the internet for the exact time using **NTP**, then keeps counting by itself. Phones and computers set their clocks the same way.
stretch: Show the date under the time (look at `tm_mday` and `tm_mon`).
Make a countdown to the end of the lesson.
Switch between 12-hour and 24-hour time with a button.
